title: Profile a Messy Invoice Inbox
scenario: It is 8:00 AM and five invoices landed overnight - more than the clean morning, and not all of them should be paid. Before you build, profile this busier inbox: who sends these, why the pile is riskier than it looks, and what the desk must be ready to catch downstream.
input: 5 documents in the AP shared mailbox. INV-59001 (Northwind Fasteners, PO-7742, $1,200.00). INV-59002 (Cascade Packaging, PO-7751, $1,230.00). INV-58962 (Northwind Fasteners, $640.00) - the number looks familiar. INV-59004 (Sierra Tooling, PO-7760, $1,200.00) - a vendor the desk does not recognize. INV-59005 (Northwind Fasteners, PO-7763, $1,000.00). Same mailbox, mixed formats, arriving on no fixed schedule.
instructions: Read the inbox as a source, not as data to extract - extraction is the Invoice Record task.
Notice that a busier inbox carries more failure modes, not just more volume.
Answer the four source questions and validate to mint the source profile.

questions.prompt: Who produces the documents in this inbox?

options.text: The AP Clerk, by typing them each morning
Vendors, who send invoices to Beacon's shared mailbox and portal

questions.explain: Invoices still originate outside Beacon - Northwind, Cascade, and an unfamiliar Sierra Tooling all sent these. The AP Clerk receives and processes them; it does not author them.

questions.prompt: Why is a five-invoice inbox riskier than a one-invoice inbox, beyond volume?

options.text: It is not - more invoices just take longer to type
Each extra invoice can carry its own failure mode - a duplicate, a bad price, an unknown vendor, a missing receipt

questions.explain: Look at the pile: a familiar-looking number, an unrecognized vendor, prices to check. A batch is where duplicates, out-of-tolerance prices, unknown vendors, and missing receipts all hide - so the desk downstream must be built to catch each one.

questions.prompt: Should the inbox itself decide which invoices are duplicates or bad?

options.text: Yes - the mailbox should reject bad invoices on arrival
No - the inbox only captures what arrived; matching and dedupe are later, owned steps
No - bad invoices should be deleted before anyone sees them

questions.explain: The source's job is faithful capture, including the bad ones. Judging them (duplicate check, three-way match, routing) happens downstream where the rules are owned and logged - never silently at the door.

questions.prompt: Which workflow step consumes these invoices first?
questions.explain: Follow the map's edge: the inbox's first stop is the Invoice Record task, which extracts every document - clean or not - into a structured record for the matching steps to judge.

artifactOnPass.producedBy: Vendors (Northwind Fasteners, Cascade Packaging, Sierra Tooling)

copilotPrompt: Profile a five-invoice AP inbox as an automation source: who produces the documents, why a batch carries more failure modes than volume, whether the inbox should judge invoices, and which workflow step consumes them first.
successMessage: Source profiled. You know the pile is mixed and some invoices should not pay - next, extract all five into structured records.

intro.heading: Before you build: a batch hides more than volume

sections.title: The clean day was the exception
sections.body: In the Easy tier one clean invoice flowed the whole desk. Real mornings look like this one: several invoices at once, and only some are payable. Profiling that reality up front is what makes the matching steps worth building.

sections.title: Every invoice is a different risk
sections.body: A batch is not one problem five times. This pile hides a duplicate, a price outside tolerance, a vendor not on file, and an invoice with no receipt. Recognizing that variety is the whole point of the Medium tier.

sections.title: Capture first, judge later
sections.body: The inbox faithfully captures everything that arrived, including the bad invoices. The desk judges them downstream where the rules are owned and every decision is logged - never silently at the door.

takeaway.heading: Messy source profiled
points: You profiled a five-invoice inbox and named its four hidden failure modes: duplicate, price over tolerance, unknown vendor, missing receipt.
A batch carries more risk than volume - each invoice can fail differently, which is exactly what the matching steps must catch.
The inbox captures everything faithfully, including invoices that should not pay; judging them is a later, owned, logged step.
Your source profile records the document count and known failure modes for the batch.
The workflow can now treat the inbox as a mixed batch where some invoices will be held rather than paid.
